pairs.why: B's drive wheels sit on the rails and are linked by rods, with a proper cowcatcher; A's front ends in a flat slab hanging down to the ties and its small front wheels don't line up with the track.
A's X-legs, armrests and seat frame all join at real pivots like a working camp chair; in B the front seat bar sticks out past the frame and the back posts don't meet the crossed legs consistently.
B's saucer is seen from one side-on camera with its rim, underside and dome agreeing; A's disc is seen from above while its dome is drawn side-on.

A's deck rests on posts, with the life ring hung from a post by its rope; B has a floating reflection of the life ring in open water, below where the ring actually is, while the rest of the pier has no matching reflection.
A is a four-wheeled wagon with its pole at the front; B shows two wheels on a lopsided bed, a seat stuck on the side and a pole jutting out of the rear side to the ground.
A's planks sit on posts in the water and the life ring and rope hang from posts; B's life ring has a stray reflection floating in open water, apart from the pier.
Both tables are buildable; B's thick top on a stepped pedestal, with solid stools, is closer to the chunky real stone table, while A's thin top on a narrow column is weaker but not wrong.
Both locomotives are coherent; B's wheels, connecting rods and tender sit clearly on the track from one camera, while A's cab and smokebox are slightly squashed together but still plausible.
